subject: Monte Carlo simulations with Lavaan and computational efficiency

messages.author: 671b14edc9322fa7
messages.subject: Monte Carlo simulations with Lavaan and computational efficiency
parts:
Hi,

I am running Monte Carlo simulations with Lavaan and would like to do this in a way that is as computationally efficient as possible. I am interested only in standardized estimates, not fit indices and not standard errors. Some of the models that I am running are not identified and this is by design (don't ask why). 

Is it possible to have direct access to the optimizer? Ideally, I would just create the model matrices and starting values once and then reuse these with different data covariance matrices. Also, I would like to abort the optimizer when it hits a flat region in the likelihood function, because this indicates a non-identified model and there is no need for further optimization. 

Mikko

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Monte Carlo simulations with Lavaan and computational efficiency
parts:
On 08/20/2014 11:18 AM, Mikko Rönkkö wrote:
> Is it possible to have direct access to the optimizer? Ideally, I would
> just create the model matrices and starting values once and then reuse
> these with different data covariance matrices.

This can be done, but (for now), you need to use lavaan's internal
functions. Have a look at the lavaan() function. You can use the
internal functions (lavData, lavaanify, lav_samplestats_from_data, etc)
to create the ingredients for the lav_model_objective() function, which
is doing the optimization of the free parameters.

> abort the optimizer when it hits a flat region in the likelihood
> function, because this indicates a non-identified model and there is no
> need for further optimization.

Currently, there is no way to 'access' the optimizer. Once it starts
(the default is nlminb()), we have no control.

You could replace the optimizer by another one. There are some
optimizers around that are written in R. These would allow you to
intervene if necessary...

Yves.
